result.title: Beyond Image-Text Pairs: Aligning Semantic Changes for Fine-Grained Visual Understanding
result.summary: Image-text alignment serves as a foundation for modern vision-language models (VLMs), yet prevailing training paradigms provide limited supervision for learning how semantic changes correspond across modalities. To address this limitation, we propose a post-training method that learns cross-modal semantic change correspondences through controlled visual and textual variations. Specifically, we introduce a Semantic Difference Alignment (SDA) loss which can align the directions of corresponding visual and textual representation changes. We combine our proposed SDA with pairwise sigmoid matching to jointly learn image-text correspondences and cross-modal semantic changes, encouraging more fine-grained and discriminative visual representations. To support this learning, we construct VarFamily-40K, a dataset of image-text pairs with controlled cross-modal semantic variations. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in compositional understanding and downstream classification performance, alongside further gains on multimodal tasks when the adapted visual encoder is integrated into VLMs.

AI.brief_summary: 提出一种后训练方法，用受控的图像与文本变体构造跨模态语义变化对应关系，通过 Semantic Difference Alignment 损失对齐两侧表示变化的方向，并结合 pairwise sigmoid matching 联合训练，同时构建 VarFamily-40K 数据集。
